chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The time of Fajr is when the dawn breaks until the morning light spreads over the sky. It is not proper to delay that intentionally, but it is still a time for one who was occupied, or forgot, or slept.

key_terms.السَّمَاءَ: the sky, indicating the spread of daylight
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the dawn; here, the start of the time of salat al-Fajr
key_terms.تَأْخِيرُ: delaying the performance of the prayer
key_terms.نَامَ: slept, referring to one who missed the earlier time due to sleep
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the appointed time or legal period for performing an act of worship
key_terms.يَنْشَقُّ: breaks open or emerges; describing the appearance of true dawn

ai.seo_question: What is the time for Fajr prayer, and is it permissible to delay it?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the time of salat al-Fajr as beginning with the break of dawn and extending until the morning light covers the sky. It also teaches that one should not intentionally delay the prayer, though this extended time remains valid for someone prevented by occupation, forgetfulness, or sleep.
